learning_outcomes.description: Apply rigorous mathematical reasoning, draw conclusions from empirical evidence, and efficiently implement relevant mathematical and statistical techniques.
Communication ideas clearly using examples, counterexamples, special cases, graphs, tables, and visualisation techniques where appropriate.
Situate findings within the contest of the field’s development, comparing and evaluating alternative approaches.
Reference original results accurately, using a consistent and appropriate bibliographic style.
Write with clarity, coherence and strong organisational structure in a consistent style.

assessments.task_description:
You will need to write a project report summarizing your research project. The report should include an accessible description of the problem background, a rigorous literature review, a thorough and rigorous description of your research methods, a detailed record of your research results, an objective comparison with existing results, and a complete, properly formatted reference list. We do not expect you to produce publishable results, so when you compare your results with existing ones, yours do not need to come out ahead every time, or even at all. There is no formal page limit, but in past practice, a report of 20-30 pages has usually been sufficient for a 2-unit project, 40-60 pages for a 4-unit project, and 80-120 pages for an 8-unit project.

Your project report is expected to reflect the time commitment associated with its unit value. For example, the same report might receive 70% in a 4-unit research project but 90% in a 2-unit research project. You are not required to follow a specific formatting or referencing style, but your presentation and citations must be clear, consistent throughout, and in line with the established standards of your discipline. If you undertake two or more coursework research projects in the same semester, you must submit a separate report for each project; the same report cannot be submitted for more than one project.

DECLARATION

A Confidentiality Agreement (CA) is not a standard requirement for research projects. A CA is required only when your research involves confidential data, intellectual property, or other sensitive materials. In such cases, your supervisor will coordinate the preparation of the agreement, explain its terms to you, and arrange for you to sign it. If you have not signed a CA, you must include one of these two declarations on the title page of your project report: "I grant permission for copies of this report to be made available as a learning resource to students enrolled at The University of Queensland." or "I do not grant permission for copies of this report to be made available as a learning resource."

MARKING

Marks are awarded on the following basis:

  • Quality of introduction /20%
  • Demonstration of understanding key elements /30% (40% for projects in Mathematics Education)
  • Rigour of definitions, proofs, calculations, etc. /20% (not for projects in Mathematics Education)
  • Appropriate style of writing /20% (30% for projects in Mathematics Education)
  • Appropriate referencing /10%

Project Defense must be scheduled during or before the last Friday of Exam Week(s), depending on the availability of student and supervisor.
assessments.task_description:
The project defense consists of a 15-minute presentation followed by a 10-minute question-and-answer session. It assesses your genuine understanding of your research project and your ability to communicate your work clearly and confidently. It is also used to clarify your individual contribution, to confirm your understanding of the key concepts, methods, and literature relevant to the project, and, as part of ensuring academic integrity, to verify that your project report reflects your own understanding and effort. During the defense, you are expected to give a concise summary of the project's objectives, methodology, and findings, and to respond thoughtfully to questions about the project's background, approach, results, and significance. You should be prepared to justify your choices, discuss alternative approaches, and reflect on the limitations and implications of your work.

Because the project defense is a hurdle, it must be recorded, and the recording must be uploaded to Blackboard by yourself. The only people required to attend are you and at least one supervisor, so you and your supervisor can schedule the defense on your own, without consulting anyone else. You or your supervisor may also invite others to attend, or expand the defense into a research seminar in the School of Mathematics and Physics or another school. The defense can be held in person, online, or in a hybrid format. If you undertake two or more coursework research projects in the same semester, you must hold a separate defense for each project; a single defense cannot cover more than one project.

This assessment item will be audio-visually recorded and retained in accordance with University requirements.
